name_reason: Already fully compliant with the global naming convention: data_fd2_ prefix, chapter domain, ch22 is a meaningful chapter ID (chapters 01-30 are domain IDs that must be preserved, not Ghidra address residue), and the descriptor reflects both purpose (end_scene_char_pos_y) and data type (table/array). No address residue in the name.
purpose: Chapter 22 end-scene world-tile Y coordinate, one byte per character slot 0..15, read by fd2_chapter_22_end to lay out the party for the post-battle cutscene.
logic_summary: 16-byte const lookup table. fd2_chapter_22_end @ 0x244B6 copies it (REP MOVSD of 4 dwords = 16 bytes) onto stack scratch, then passes the stack copy as arg2/pos_y to fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro, which indexes it by char slot to set each placed char's world Y tile. Values: 0x16,0x14,0x16,0x16,0x17,0x17,0x17,0x17,0x17,0x18,0x18,0x18,0x18,0x18,0x19,0x19. Sibling tables: pos_x @ 0x52273, facing @ 0x52293.
element_semantics: table[slot] = world-tile Y coordinate for character slot `slot` (0..15) during the chapter-22 end-scene placement. Each element is a tile-Y value (range 0x14..0x19 observed).
notes: Reader confirms the access pattern via both decompile and disasm (000244de MOV ESI,0x52283 ; 000244e3 MOVSD.REP, ECX=4). xrefs_to show only READ + DATA refs from fd2_chapter_22_end (no writers) => is_const confirmed. src/field/chend2.c lines 260-279 already document all three ch22 end-scene tables (x/y/facing) collectively and accurately, with correct values for the pos_y member (lines 272-275, byte-matching memory) -> comment kept, no src Edit needed. Ghidra plate for 0x52283 was null/empty; created a per-table plate consistent with the sibling pos_x plate @ 0x52273 and with the src conclusion. src/field/chend2.c had no diff (untouched), so the only staged artifact besides the shard is none -- shard only.
